entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Jan Očko of Vlašim (Unknown–1380) was the second Archbishop of Prague, a pivotal figure in the 14th-century Czech Reformation.




Očko, a member of the influential House of Vlašim, played a crucial role in the Council of Basel (1431–1449), where he advocated for the inclusion of the Czech people in the church's governance. This stance ultimately led to the establishment of the Union of the Bohemian Brethren (1451), a Protestant sect that shaped the religious landscape of the region.





As Archbishop, Očko oversaw the construction of the iconic St. Vitus Cathedral in Prague, which became a symbol of the city's spiritual and cultural rebirth. His legacy extends beyond his ecclesiastical achievements, as he also contributed to the development of the Czech language and literature.




Očko's significance lies in his ability to bridge the gap between the Catholic Church and the emerging Protestant movement, paving the way for the Czech Reformation's impact on European religious history.

entities.name: Jan Očko of Vlašim
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Jan Očko of Vlašim (from the House of Vlašim) was the second Archbishop of Prague (1364–1378), succeeding Arnošt of Pardubice in the young metropolitan see created under Charles IV. As Prague's archbishop in the Luxembourg golden age, he stood at the junction of imperial court culture, Bohemian church reform, and the political theology of a capital that Charles was remaking into a New Jerusalem of central Europe.

Očko crowned and counselled within a church still consolidating its archiepiscopal rights, managing cathedral chapter, diocesan discipline, and relations with the papacy during the Avignon period's endgame and the onset of schism. His tenure framed the ecclesiastical stage on which later Bohemian controversies—including those leading toward Hus—would unfold.

Art and memory also preserve him: donor portraits and Prague castle–cathedral culture mark the Vlašim archbishop as a pillar of Charles IV's sacral kingship.
